name: Adriano Santos
headline: 48, retired percussionist and theater technician, Rio de Janeiro
title: The Roda de Samba Invitation
situation: Adriano is in his garage repairing a drum shell when his old friend Marcos appears at the gate, holding two bottles of beer. Marcos says his neighborhood samba group is hosting a roda de samba tonight at a neighbor's house, and he wants Adriano to come along just to listen, not play. Marcos adds that everyone remembers his surdo technique and it's been too long. Adriano feels his usual reluctance toward group gatherings, but Marcos is one of the few friends who still visits. He must answer now.

context.relationship_profiles:
Marcos is his oldest surviving friend from the early block parties; they played surdo together for over a decade.
Marcos visits about once a month, never mentions the accident unless Adriano brings it up.
Adriano trusts Marcos but still keeps him at arm's length because Marcos organizes community events.
context.tendencies:
When neighbors invite him to street events, he usually declines politely and then spends the evening commenting on their videos.
Twice in the past year he accepted a close friend's visit but set a strict time limit and left early.
He rarely joins anything that requires a group commitment, preferring to observe from a distance.
context.current_state:
He has been in the garage since 8 a.m., replacing lugs on a 1980s kit; his hands ache and his right ear throbs from the intermittent compressor noise.
He didn't sleep well and hasn't cooked dinner, but he feels steady in his routine.
He hadn't spoken to anyone all day.
context.immediate_memories:
The beer bottles recall the afternoon after his accident when Marcos brought the same brand and sat with him silently for two hours.
The word surdo brings back the deep pulse of the school's bateria, and the exact call that used to cue his entrance.
Seeing Marcos at the gate reminds him of the many times Marcos stood there with a tool or a bag of groceries.
context.reflective_memories:
He has avoided municipal arts meetings for years, remembering the annual funding debates that ended in applause and no new equipment.
He also remembers that the best sound check he ever had was in an informal roda with no microphones and no leadership, just a circle of friends.
He has often told online viewers that live samba's authenticity depends on being in the room, not watching a screen.
